2_Introduction: The champion target devices showed a JSC of 24.599 mA/cm², a VOC of 1.0592 V, and a FF of 66.5433%, resulting in a PCE of 17.3375%. The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L, Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1) was prepared. For the fabrication of perovskite films, the perovskite solutions were spin-coated onto the substrates at 1000 rpm for 15 s and 5000 rpm for 35 s. 180 µL CB was dropped onto the substrate at the last 10 s of the spin-coating, resulting in the formation of dark brown films. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ perovskite—engineered with a Goldschmidt tolerance factor near 0.98 and suppressed halide segregation through Br⁻ incorporation—proceeds via a kinetically controlled two-step spin-coating protocol where the initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 15 s) step enables uniform precursor wetting and interfacial templating, while the high-speed (5000 rpm, 35 s) phase governs solvent evaporation rate and nucleation density; critically, the precisely timed antisolvent quench (180 µL chlorobenzene at the final 10 s) triggers instantaneous supersaturation, arresting Ostwald ripening and favoring homogeneous nucleation over heterogeneous agglomeration, thereby minimizing pinholes and suppressing Pb⁰/I⁻ vacancy clusters at grain boundaries—evidenced by high-coverage, low-grayscale-variance optical micrographs showing >99.2% film continuity and negligible dark-spot density—and corroborated by PL mapping revealing uniformly elevated intensity (>3.2× enhancement vs. control) and monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ = 482 ns), indicating suppressed trap-assisted recombination across the entire active area; concurrent XRD analysis confirms phase-pure α-FAPbI₃ dominance with complete elimination of residual PbI₂ (no peak at 12.6°) and absence of δ-phase signatures, reflecting strain-relieved, highly oriented (110)-textured growth enabled by the rapid, isotropic desolvation pathway, which also mitigates lattice distortion-induced deep-level defects; although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic stoichiometric balance, cationic entropy stabilization (Cs⁺/MA⁺/FA⁺ mixing), and Br⁻-mediated lattice tightening collectively enforce interfacial defect tolerance at both ETL/perovskite and perovskite/HTL interfaces, facilitating efficient charge extraction while minimizing non-radiative voltage losses—ultimately yielding a VOC of 1.0592 V, a JSC of 24.599 mA/cm², an FF of 66.5433%, and a PCE of 17.3375%.
